title: Meet Redbelly
audience: Someone with no crypto knowledge: a friend, a parent or a business owner.

posts.text:
Redbelly in one sentence: a public network, built in Australia, where real financial assets like bonds, investment funds and loans can be issued, managed and traded as digital items, with ID checks and the rules built in.

Here is why that matters. 1/9

image.alt: Title card on a dark slate background. Small label: Meet Redbelly. Headline: Real assets. Verified people. Rules built in. Below it: Redbelly is a public network, built in Australia, where bonds, investment funds and loans can be issued, managed and traded as digital items. Footer: Facts last verified 30 October 2026, with the Redbelly DAO logo in the corner.

claims.text: Redbelly is a public network.
Redbelly was built in Australia.
Financial assets such as bonds, investment funds and loans can be issued, managed and traded on it.
ID checks and the asset's rules are built in.

posts.text: Start with the problem. Buying into a bond or a fund today means money and paperwork passing between several companies. Each one keeps its own records, and they all have to be matched up, sometimes by hand. That costs time and money. 2/9

image.alt: Side by side comparison titled: Many sets of records, or one network. Left panel, Today: three boxes, Company A, Company B and Company C, each with its own records, joined by lines marked: match up, sometimes by hand. Below: time and cost spent checking. Right panel, On Redbelly: one network, where the people using it are verified. Three points: the asset and the money can move together, rules checked automatically, final once confirmed.

claims.text: In traditional finance, several institutions keep separate records that must be reconciled, which can need manual work and costs money.

posts.text:
Now picture a digital concert ticket. It proves the seat is yours, it moves to a new owner in seconds, and the venue sets the rules on who can resell it.

Redbelly lets financial assets work the same way. In finance, this is called tokenisation. 3/9

image.alt: Two cards compared row by row. Left card, Concert ticket: proves seat 14B is yours, moves to a new owner in seconds, rules set by the venue, held by whoever the venue allows. Right card, Digital fund unit: proves 1 unit of Example Fund is yours, can settle instantly, rules set by the issuer and checked automatically, held by verified, eligible investors. Footer: Illustrative example. Example Fund is not a real product.

claims.text: Tokenisation records ownership of a financial asset as a digital item and lets the issuer program the asset's rules.
Redbelly is infrastructure for issuing and moving these digital financial assets.

posts.text: The part most people miss: Redbelly is designed so the people using it are verified. Each transfer can be checked against the asset's rules automatically. And privacy tech is used so that being verified does not mean showing everyone your personal details. 4/9

claims.text: Redbelly is designed so that participants are known and verified.
Transfers can be checked against the asset's rules automatically.
Privacy technology (zero-knowledge proofs) protects participants' privacy while they are verified.

posts.text: So who keeps the records straight? No single computer gets the final say. A group of computers must agree on every transaction, using a voting method developed at the University of Sydney. Once something is confirmed, it is final, and everyone sees the same version. 5/9

claims.text: No single computer controls the outcome; agreement is reached through a democratic process.
The agreement method (DBFT) was developed at the University of Sydney.
Confirmed transactions are final and there is one consistent record, with no forking.

posts.text: Where it comes from: Redbelly grew out of research at the University of Sydney and CSIRO, Australia's national science agency. The live network launched in November 2024. Tokeniser, a Redbelly Network project, runs on it for Australian funds and companies. 6/9

claims.text: Redbelly came out of research at the University of Sydney and CSIRO.
CSIRO is Australia's national science agency.
The live network (mainnet) launched in November 2024.
Tokeniser is a Redbelly Network project that operates on Redbelly Network and is built for Australian funds and companies.

posts.text: It has also been used in a central bank project. Project Acacia, run by the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Digital Finance CRC, used Redbelly as one of its networks, including for pilot digital money from the central bank. The final report came out in May 2026. 7/9

image.alt: Fact card titled Project Acacia: a research project of the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Digital Finance Cooperative Research Centre. Four facts with status dots: Redbelly was one of the networks used for pilot use cases. Pilot digital central bank money was used on Redbelly for testing. Use cases on Redbelly were led by Australian Bond Exchange, Fireblocks, Macropod and NotCentralised. Final report published May 2026. Footer: Research, not an endorsement. The RBA does not endorse any participant. Facts last verified 30 October 2026. Source: RBA and DFCRC, Project Acacia final report, May 2026.

claims.text: The Reserve Bank of Australia is Australia's central bank.
Project Acacia is a joint initiative of the RBA and the Digital Finance Cooperative Research Centre.
Redbelly Network was one of the networks used for Project Acacia pilot use cases.
Pilot wholesale central bank digital currency was used on Redbelly Network in the project.
The final report was released in May 2026.

posts.text: On Redbelly, teams led by Australian Bond Exchange, Fireblocks, Macropod and NotCentralised tested things like corporate bonds, an investment fund and a security backed by loans. To be clear: this was research, and the RBA does not endorse any participant. 8/9

claims.text: Use cases (trials) led by ABE, Macropod, Fireblocks and NotCentralised ran on Redbelly.
Those use cases covered corporate bonds, an investment fund and a security backed by loans.
Project Acacia was research, and the RBA does not endorse any participant.

posts.text:
Why it matters:
Businesses can raise money and manage investors digitally, with the rules built in.
Trades can settle instantly.
The money and the asset can move together, with less back and forth.

Real assets, verified people, rules built in.

redbelly.network 9/9

Trades can settle instantly.
Money and assets can sit on the same network and move together, reducing reconciliation.
